content: Hello! how can I help today?
I have rental losses but too much AGI to deduct them. Any way around this?
Yes. If you qualify as a **Real Estate Professional** under **IRC §469(c)(7)**, your rental losses become **non-passive** and fully deductible against other income.

1. You must spend **>750 hours** per year in real estate activities
2. You must spend **>50% of your working time** in real estate
3. Make an **election under Reg. §1.469-9(g)** to aggregate rentals
Include a statement with your **Form 1040** that declares your aggregation election under **Reg. 1.469-9(g)**. Once made, it applies until revoked with IRS consent.
Can I retroactively make this election?
Yes—with a **reasonable cause statement** under **Rev. Proc. 2011-34**, you can file the late election and treat rentals as non-passive if IRS accepts.
